claims.text: The hypothesis applies to Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with density below 6 g/cm³.
The initial alloy contains both solid-solution regions and intermetallic compounds.
The phases in the initial alloy are metastable.
The initial mixed-phase microstructure is produced by induction melting.
A controlled post-processing thermal treatment will transform the initial microstructure into a more homogenized and refined phase distribution.
Unstable intermetallic precipitates will dissolve or re-precipitate more finely during the thermal treatment.
The thermal treatment will produce Al enrichment at grain boundaries and alloy surfaces.
Surface enrichment in protective elements can produce a passivating surface film in an Mg-containing multi-principal-element alloy.
The enriched surface will nucleate and grow a continuous, dense, and adherent protective oxide film under oxidizing exposure.
The protective surface film will retard corrosive attack.
The protective oxide scale will retard scale spallation and improve high-temperature oxidation stability.
Relative to isotropic cooling without post-treatment, the treated alloy will have lower corrosion current density.
Relative to isotropic cooling without post-treatment, the treated alloy will have a higher corrosion potential.
Relative to isotropic cooling without post-treatment, the treated alloy will exhibit a reduced mass change during high-temperature oxidation.
XRD and SEM will reveal a continuous, adherent oxide scale on the treated alloy.
The proposed behavior is expected to apply during oxidation at temperatures up to approximately 900 °C.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy can be used to measure corrosion current density and corrosion potential in the proposed comparison.
The exact transformation kinetics, oxide composition, oxide thickness, and quantitative property improvements remain uncertain and depend on thermal-treatment parameters.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies exposure to aggressive corrosive electrolytes, whereas the boundary limits the hypothesis to moderate corrosive media.
